family.description: This family contains members from all branches of life. The molecular function of this protein is unknown, but Memo (mediator of ErbB2-driven cell motility) a human protein is included in this family [[cite:PUB00044702]]. It has been suggested that Memo controls cell migration by relaying extracellular chemotactic signals to the microtubule cytoskeleton [[cite:PUB00044702]].
family.name: Memo-like protein

history.description: Eleven graphs retain sixteen observed effects from four primary studies, six direct preparation-level and ten indirect cellular effects. history.description: Scoped same-agent scientific review retains eleven graphs and sixteen observed effects with verified reference/domain mapping, primary Methods and original figures. history.summary: Review Memo metal binding redox and cellular causal contexts

causal_graphs.context: N2 glovebox stocks; CuCl stock stabilized with ascorbate; BCA to Cu ratio 2.5. Figure1 says 10 uM Cu; supplementary Methods says 20 uM Cu and 50 uM BCA for Memo1. This discrepancy remains unresolved.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure1C/D and supplementary Methods pp4-5; retain the 10/20-uM discrepancy and model-dependent stoichiometry rather than silently choosing a concentration or microscopic affinity.

edges.mechanism: Increasing the protein concentration lowers the preformed copper-chelator chromophore. Reverse competition and retained ICP-MS observations support metal binding; they do not identify an enzymatic substrate or a physiological transfer direction.
edges.subject: add-memo1

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Human Q9Y316 sequence version1 equals NP_057039.1/NM_015955.5, 297 aa, PF01875 8-291. pET28a/BL21(DE3), His-affinity and SEC preparation, Western identity check; exact insert and tag cleavage are not independently verified. Whole preparation, not isolated domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Decreased chromophore supports competition for Cu(I), not catalysis. Two equal-affinity sites and 4e-15 M are model assumptions/estimate; unequal sites remain possible. Do not compare directly with glutathione-containing 2024 ITC affinities.

nodes.label: Increase purified Memo1 in the Cu(I)-BCA2 mixture

causal_graphs.scope: Zhang2022 Figure1C/D, human Memo1 added to preformed Cu(I)-BCA2 under anaerobic conditions.
causal_graphs.title: Purified Memo1 competes for reduced copper in a BCA assay

causal_graphs.context: 8 uM Memo1, 35 uM ascorbate, 4 or 8 uM Cu(II), 25 mM HEPES pH7.4, 200 mM NaCl, air, room temperature; A265 every 2 min through 20 min.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure2A and supplement pp5-6; no-copper/protein controls and distinct 35-uM ascorbate concentration are retained.

edges.mechanism: Protein-containing reactions retain substantially more A265 signal than copper-containing no-protein reactions. The measured protection applies to these component ratios and is not proof that every reported Memo redox assay is artifactual.
edges.subject: memo1-with-copper-and-ascorbate

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Human pET28a Memo1 preparation assigned to Q9Y316/NP_057039.1, PF01875 8-291. His-affinity purified; no tag removal is described in inspected Methods. Not the 2014 3C-cleaved or 2024 intein-cleaved preparation.
causal_graphs.limitations: This is the supplied copper/reductant protocol, not universal antioxidant activity. Higher Cu to protein ratios precipitate. Binding/chelation explains the result but no atomistic redox trajectory is directly observed.

nodes.label: Add Memo1 to copper and ascorbate in air
Ascorbate consumption inferred from A265 loss

causal_graphs.scope: Zhang2022 Figure2A, purified Memo1 versus no protein in matched copper/ascorbate reactions.
causal_graphs.title: Memo1 reduces copper-dependent ascorbate consumption

causal_graphs.context: 8 uM Memo1, 50 uM ascorbate, 50 uM Amplex Red, 3.55 U/ml HRP, 4 or 8 uM Cu(II), 100 ul; fluorescence followed through 60 min. Main legend gives 571/585 nm; supplement gives 544/590 nm.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure2B and supplementary p6; background signal, reagent conjunction and wavelength inconsistency constrain the interpretation.

edges.mechanism: Adding Memo1 lowers the reporter signal relative to copper/ascorbate without protein. The independent ascorbate experiment supports protection against redox cycling, but this edge preserves the actual coupled-assay readout.
edges.subject: memo1-in-coupled-reaction

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Human pET28a Memo1 preparation, Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference, PF01875 8-291. Exact tag and batch sequence remain unverified; whole preparation, not domain-only chemistry.
causal_graphs.limitations: Wavelength disagreement remains open. The endpoint is a coupled HRP/probe signal; no independent interference control was verified. Low signal is near protein-only background, not literally zero fluorescence or proof of zero ROS of every kind.

nodes.label: Add Memo1 to the copper/ascorbate/HRP/Amplex mixture

causal_graphs.scope: Zhang2022 Figure2B, matched purified-protein versus no-protein reactions.
causal_graphs.title: Memo1 lowers the copper-dependent Amplex Red readout

causal_graphs.context: 50 uM CuCl2, luminol detection, matched no-Cu and 4-U SOD controls; four independent experiments. Protein amount for this unpreloaded panel is not independently resolved; the separate preloading recipe is not silently substituted.

evidence.explanation: Reprinted Figure4D and printed pp105-107 Methods; preserve residual activity, uncertain panel protein dose and alternative explanations from later work. Kinetic Km is not an equilibrium binding Kd.

edges.mechanism: The H192A preparation produces less luminol signal than WT in the Cu-containing comparison; SOD decreases both. Reporter dependence is retained without deciding that the protein alone catalyzes the proposed redox cycle.
edges.subject: h192a

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Human cDNA in pOPINF/BL21(DE3), Ni-NTA, 3C cleavage and SEC. Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference maps PF01875 8-291 and H192 inside; exact batch sequence and residual tag are not independently verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: H192A retains substantial signal. This is an observed preparation-dependent reporter effect, not unqualified intrinsic Cu(II)-reductase activity. The older catalytic interpretation is disputed by later protection results under different conditions. No matched 2014 folding/metal-occupancy control was verified.

nodes.label: Replace WT Memo with H192A in the copper-containing assay

causal_graphs.scope: MacDonald2014 Figure4D, WT versus H192A recombinant human Memo, author thesis reprint printed p119/PDFp122.
causal_graphs.title: H192A lowers the historical copper-containing luminol response

causal_graphs.context: DMEM with 10% heat-inactivated FBS, 37 C/5% CO2; 1e5 cells/24-well, siRNA 24 h after seeding, scratch 24 h later; ImageJ recovered area at 24 h after scratching. Four-siRNA Qiagen pool, RNAiMAX, Western/actin control.

evidence.explanation: Original supplementary FigureS1 and Methods pp6-7; ten micrographs are not silently treated as ten independent biological experiments.

edges.mechanism: Knockdown cultures recover less wound area than negative-control cultures at the shared 24-hour time point. This does not independently measure migration speed or resolve a cytoskeletal pathway.
edges.subject: simemo1

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Endogenous human MEMO1 locus, Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference, PF01875 8-291. Whole-protein depletion, not isolated-domain perturbation; exact siRNA sequence/dose and batch genotype are not verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: Wound closure can include proliferation as well as migration. No proliferation block or rescue was verified. Methods lists 8/12/24 h, caption 8/24 h and plot 8/24/48 h; only the common 24-hour comparison is retained.
causal_graphs.scope: Zhang2022 Supplementary FigureS1, MDA-MB-231 siMemo1 versus AllStars siCtrl.
causal_graphs.title: Memo1 knockdown reduces 24-hour wound closure

causal_graphs.context: Four-siRNA Qiagen pool/RNAiMAX, AllStars control, Western-confirmed 70-80% knockdown; 1e4 cells/well seeded 24 h, CuCl2 exposure 18 h, MTT 4 h in serum-free medium, DMSO and A570.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure1A and main Methods, PDFpp3/5; preserve the metabolic endpoint and matched350-uM comparison rather than equating lower signal with measured death rate.

edges.mechanism: At matched external copper concentration the knockdown has lower MTT signal than siCtrl. The broader titration includes a basal knockdown effect and does not isolate copper-specific death or an intracellular chelation mechanism.
edges.subject: simemo1-with-copper

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Human endogenous MEMO1, Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference and PF01875 8-291. Not complete knockout or an isolated-domain assay; exact siRNA sequences/dose and interval before assay are not specified in inspected Methods.
causal_graphs.limitations: MTT measures metabolic viability, not direct cell-death counts. Knockdown also lowers signal without added Cu; a Cu-specific statistical interaction is not established. Two biological repeats and four technical replicates per condition; no rescue verified.

nodes.label: Knock down Memo1 during 350-uM CuCl2 exposure

causal_graphs.scope: Zhang2023 Figure1A, MDA-MB-231 siMemo1 versus siCtrl at matched 350 uM external CuCl2.
causal_graphs.title: Memo1 knockdown lowers MTT signal during copper exposure

causal_graphs.context: Same pooled-siRNA protocol and 70-80% Western reduction. Separate ROS-Glo, CellROX Green and MitoSOX Red assays, two biological repeats with four technical replicates per condition. ROS-Glo substrate incubates another 6 h, then detection reagent 20 min.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure2, PDFp3, and ROS-Glo Methods p5; basal no-Cu comparison is not significant and is not generalized into this edge.

edges.mechanism: Knockdown increases the peroxide-linked luminescence in both biological repeats under high external copper. The substrate-incubation period prevents treating this as an instantaneous 18-hour peroxide concentration.
edges.subject: simemo1-with-copper

evidence.explanation: Original Figure3A-C and Methods; 5 uM CellROX for30 min, approximately1e4 cells per flow sample. Probe specificity and localization remain limits.

edges.mechanism: CellROX Green fluorescence increases with Memo1 knockdown at the matched copper exposure in both repeats. The result is a bulk cellular probe readout, not the localized protrusion signal examined in older work.
edges.subject: simemo1-with-copper

evidence.explanation: Original Figure3D-F and Methods; 5 uM probe for10 min, approximately6000 cells per sample. Basal behavior differs between repeats and is not asserted as a uniform effect.

edges.mechanism: MitoSOX Red fluorescence increases under the high-copper knockdown condition in both repeats. This does not identify the oxidized probe product or directly quantify mitochondrial superoxide production rate.
edges.subject: simemo1-with-copper

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Endogenous human MEMO1, Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference, PF01875 8-291. Whole-protein knockdown with unresolved individual siRNA specificity, not domain-specific chemistry.
causal_graphs.limitations: Probe signals are not product-resolved ROS chemistry or molecular production rates. At zero added Cu, ROS-Glo is unchanged and MitoSOX differs in only one repeat; CellROX differs in both. No direct intracellular Cu flux, chelation or Atox1 epistasis is demonstrated.

nodes.label: Knock down Memo1 during 350-uM CuCl2 exposure

causal_graphs.scope: Zhang2023 Figures2/3, MDA-MB-231 siMemo1 versus siCtrl, 350 uM external CuCl2 for 18 h.
causal_graphs.title: Memo1 knockdown increases three copper-conditioned probe responses

causal_graphs.context: 25 C ITC, 25 uM protein, 0.5 mM FeSO4 titrant, 50 mM HEPES pH7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 9.5 mM GSH/0.5 mM GSSG under argon;1.5-2.5 ul injections300 s apart; dilution-heat subtraction.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure5A and Figure5 supplement1, with ITC and purification Methods; NMR is from the2024 preparation,not retrospective validation of2014 protein.

edges.mechanism: H49A lacks the WT-like saturating binding response in the glutathione-containing iron titration. Structural coordination and folded-state NMR support involvement of this residue without proving catalytic necessity.
edges.subject: h49a

evidence.explanation: Original Figure5A and folded-state Figure5 supplement1; preserve the glutathione competition context and residual response limits rather than assert an unmeasured affinity.

edges.mechanism: C244S likewise lacks the WT-like calorimetric response. The substitution effect supports iron-site involvement,not an established oxygenase substrate or molecular turnover step.
edges.subject: c244s

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q9Y316/NP_057039.1, PF01875 8-291. Deposited 7KQ8 entity1 is exactly canonical4-297, not full297 aa. pTYB12 intein-cleaved preparation; H49/C244 use native reference numbering and lie inside the Pfam match. Assay-batch N termini are not independently sequenced.
causal_graphs.limitations: NMR supports folded mutants but not identical local geometry. Loss of detectable ITC binding response does not establish infinite Kd or loss of a known enzymatic reaction. WT apparent Kd5.0+/-2.6 uM is conditional on glutathione; H192A/D189N retain binding.

Substitute C244S in the purified protein

causal_graphs.scope: Dolgova2024 Figure5A, independently purified WT and mutant human MEMO1 preparations.
causal_graphs.title: H49A and C244S reduce the iron-binding calorimetric response

causal_graphs.context: CRISPR crRNAs target exons4-6, limiting dilution and Western validation; DMEM10%FBS. ICP-MS fractions normalized by protein; MDA kit in separate80%-confluent60-mm cultures. M67-2 knockdown is not pooled with knockout.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure4A and fractionation/ICP-MS Methods; the variable M67-2 knockdown result is not treated as another significant knockout measurement.

edges.mechanism: M67-9 contains less measured iron per protein in the cytosolic fraction than the parental line. The comparison does not identify import,export,storage or proliferation as the direct intermediate.
edges.subject: memo1-knockout

evidence.explanation: Original Figure4B and differential-centrifugation Methods; retain crude-fraction qualification and absence of flux measurement.

edges.mechanism: The crude mitochondrial fraction also has less iron per protein in M67-9. This is a compartment-enriched measurement,not purified-mitochondrial iron transport or an observed mitoferrin reaction.
edges.subject: memo1-knockout

evidence.explanation: Original Figure4F and MDA Methods; M67-2 knockdown is stronger than M67-9,while melanoma effects differ. This is a basal product measurement,not oxidation measured during RSL3 exposure.

edges.mechanism: Basal MDA per protein is higher in knockout than parental breast cancer cells. This endpoint must not be inverted to fit a proposed lower-iron/lower-oxidation explanation of drug tolerance.
edges.subject: memo1-knockout

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Endogenous human MEMO1 locus, Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference, PF01875 8-291. Whole-gene perturbation, not domain-specific chemistry; exact clonal alleles and complementation are not independently verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: Six biological replicates are specified for ICP-MS. The mitochondrial fraction is crude; reduced iron is not measured transport flux. Basal MDA increases despite lower iron and greater RSL3 tolerance,so no monotonic iron-to-lipid-oxidation-to-death chain is inferred.

causal_graphs.title: MEMO1 knockout changes basal iron fractions and lipid-oxidation product

causal_graphs.context: 1000 cells/well, RSL3 added next day for48 h, then88 uM resazurin overnight; excitation540/emission590 nm. Each line's dose response is normalized; high-dose convergence is retained.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure4E and RSL3/resazurin Methods; high-dose convergence and assay normalization qualify the direction of the effect.

edges.mechanism: Knockout cultures retain a higher normalized metabolic signal across intermediate drug doses than parental cells. No serial iron-to-lipid-oxidation-to-survival trajectory or universal resistance is inferred.
edges.subject: knockout-with-rsl3

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Human MEMO1 whole-gene CRISPR clone M67-9, Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference, PF01875 8-291. No rescue, exact allele sequence or domain-only perturbation verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: This reports normalized metabolic viability,not a direct death rate or an independently isolated ferroptosis step. It does not hold at every dose; A-375 curves are a different context. Lower iron and higher basal MDA were measured separately.

nodes.label: Use M67-9 knockout cells during matched RSL3 exposure

causal_graphs.scope: Dolgova2024 Figure4E, MDA-MB-231 parental versus M67-9, intermediate RSL3 doses in the plotted response range.
causal_graphs.title: MEMO1 knockout increases the normalized metabolic signal during RSL3 exposure

causal_graphs.context: Overnight DFX exposure, GRP75 immunostaining and separate live MitoTracker CM-H2Ros imaging; untreated cultures provide basal morphology controls.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure4D and imaging Methods; retain overnight conditional exposure and distinction between fixed GRP75 and live MitoTracker observations.

edges.mechanism: The chelator-exposed knockout displays perinuclear clustering compared with similarly exposed parental cells,whereas basal distributions are relatively normal. Concordant stains support the morphology endpoint without resolving the molecular intermediate.
edges.subject: knockout-with-dfx

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Endogenous human MEMO1 knockout, Q9Y316/NP_057039.1 reference, PF01875 8-291. Whole-gene intervention; exact clone alleles and complementation remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: Qualitative microscopy,not quantified mitochondrial transport or respiration. Basal mitochondrial distributions appear normal. Knockout and DFX form the conditional intervention; neither is asserted independently sufficient for the same phenotype.
causal_graphs.scope: Dolgova2024 Figure4D, M67-9 versus parental MDA-MB-231 in1 uM deferoxamine overnight.
causal_graphs.title: MEMO1 knockout enhances mitochondrial clustering under iron chelation

It has been suggested that Memo controls cell migration by relaying extracellular chemotactic signals to the microtubule cytoskeleton [[cite:PUB00044702]].

evidence.explanation: Figure4D supports H192A-dependent signal reduction,not an unqualified enzyme mechanism. Figure4F efficiency values do not support prose implying a superior WT kcat/Km.
Low-ratio copper assays support protection; proposed free-Cu/precipitation explanations do not directly diagnose the older preparation.

discussions.notes: Compare matched tag-cleaved proteins,folding,metal occupancy,Cu ratios,redox buffers and orthogonal products. Resolve BCA10/20-uM and Amplex wavelength discrepancies. Atox1 proximity is not directed intracellular metal flux; model-based Cu affinities and GSH-conditioned Fe affinities are not interchangeable.
discussions.prompt: Resolve preparation and assay differences before assigning a conserved Memo redox reaction.
discussions.rationale: Older luminol/Cu-reduction interpretation differs from later copper protection and glutathione-conditioned iron binding. Binding,reporter effects and cellular phenotypes are separate observations,not one proven catalytic cycle.

evidence.explanation: Basal MDA increases despite lower iron and higher RSL3 metabolic viability. These separate assays do not demonstrate a linear ferroptosis mechanism.
